questions.question: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select No error’, Never put of / until tomorrow what / you can do today.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select No error’,

Never put of / until tomorrow what / you can do today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. 'Never put of'.
Key Points
  • The error lies in the phrasal verb "put of".
  • The correct phrasal verb should be "put off" which means to delay or postpone.
  • The segment "Never put of" should be corrected to "Never put off".
  • Using "of" instead of "off" alters the intended meaning of the phrase.
Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today'.
 Additional Information
  • "You can do today" and "until tomorrow what" are correct in the context of the sentence.
  • "Off" (बंद) in this context is a preposition indicating a change in position or state, while "of" (का) indicates belonging or association.

options.text: the watchkeepers were very, very tired,
options.html: the watchkeepers were very, very tired,

questions.solution: The subject "everyone" is singular, but the verb "were" is incorrect as it is the past tense of "be" and should be replaced with "was" to agree with the singular "everyone." “Everyone” is treated as singular pronoun, so it's always used with a singular verb form. Example: Everyone is responsible for this failure. The correct sentence would be "Although people had been on watch and the watchkeepers were very, very tired, everyone was up and buzzing."

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. The little boy complained me about his careless nanny.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

The little boy complained me about his careless nanny.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'complained me'.

Key Points

  • 'Complain' is a verb which means "​to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/something".
    • E.g. Poor residents complained to the police.
  • 'Complain' is followed by the preposition 'to', when the person to whom you are complaining is mentioned.
    • E.g. I complained to the customer service representative.
  • According to the rule and example that are given above, 'complained to me' will be used instead of 'complained me'.
     

Correct Sentence: The little boy complained to me about his careless nanny.

Additional Information

  • Difference between complain and complaint-
    • 'Complain' is a verb which means "​to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/something".
      • E.g. Tourists complained about the lack of toilet facilities in the area.
    • 'Complaint' is a noun which means "a statement that somebody makes saying that they are not satisfied".
      • E.g. The most common complaint is about poor service.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Until I was / still a little weak, / I decided to walk home / from the metro station.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

Until I was / still a little weak, / I decided to walk home / from the metro station.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Until I was'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'I was' should be used instead of 'Until I was'.
  • Until is a preposition and a conjunction. Until is often shortened to till or 'til'. Till and 'til' are more informal and we don't usually use them in formal writing.
  • In the given sentence 'until' should not be used. Until as a preposition means 'up to (the time that)'.
    • Example: We played chess until midnight.
  • The use of 'until' and 'still' in the same clause is grammatically incorrect.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 2.
     

Correct Sentence: I was still a little weak, I decided to walk home from the metro station.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहाँ 'Until I was' के स्थान पर 'I was' का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
  • 'Until' एक preposition और एक conjunction है। Till और til अधिक अनौपचारिक हैं और हम आमतौर पर औपचारिक लेखन में उनका उपयोग नहीं करते हैं।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में 'until' का प्रयोग नहीं करना चाहिए। 'Until' एक preposition है जिसका अर्थ है '(उस समय तक)'।
    • Example: We played chess until midnight.​
  • एक ही clause में 'until' और 'still' का प्रयोग व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत है।
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।

  • "Industry revenue" is not a specific singular countable noun that requires an article.
  • The correct phrase should be "contributor to industry revenue," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 3 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "In the recent past, the IT industry has emerged as a major contributor to industry revenue as well as employment opportunity provider in the country."
 
Additional Information
  • "In the recent past, the IT industry has emerged" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • "as a major contributor to industry revenue" – This is the correct form after the correction.
  • "as well as employment" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • "opportunity provider in the country." – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. Early, during December 2021, / Lal was appointed / the Secretary to the Lokpal.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Early, during December 2021, / Lal was appointed / the Secretary to the Lokpal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'
Key Points
  • The time reference 'Early, during December 2021' is incorrect. It doesn't properly specify when the appointment happened.
  • Rather than saying 'Early, during December 2021,' it would be correct to say 'early in December 2021' or 'during December 2021.'
  • The word 'early' doesn't need the accompaniment of 'during.'
  • Therefore, the correct segment should be 'Early in December 2021' or 'In early December 2021', which clearly represents the period at the beginning of December.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Last night’s / Christmas party was fun. / I wish / you would come.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Last night’s / Christmas party was fun. / I wish / you would come.
questions.solution: The error lies in the part 'you would come'. In the given sentence, the action 'Christmas party' took place 'Last night' which implies that the action took place in the past. According to the rules of tense, 'I wish you would come' should be used when incident is occurring in the present. In the given sentence we need to use 'you had come' in place of 'you would come' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

questions.solution: In the given sentence, the usage of the past tense of the verb 'receive' which is "received" is grammatically incorrect. In the given sentence, the subject pronoun "she" should be followed by the conjugation of the verb "receive" which is "receives". The correct sentence is: Suchitra will have to wait another month before she receives any reply to her letter.
